main.title: Final Fantasy XIII
main.subtitle: An escape that teaches you to change roles
main.summary: On December 17, 2009, Final Fantasy XIII was released in Japan on PlayStation 3; the North American and European release would follow on March 9, 2010, also on Xbox 360.

cards.heading: A new Final Fantasy in high definition
cards.text: Final Fantasy XIII launched for PlayStation 3 in Japan on December 17, 2009. North America and Europe followed on March 9, 2010, also on Xbox 360. Square Enix builds its fast battles around switching party roles. The early journey follows tightly controlled routes before Gran Pulse opens more space for exploration and missions.

cards.heading: Changing the party's Paradigm
cards.text: Characters take roles such as Commando, Ravager, Medic and Sentinel. The player prepares combinations called Paradigms and switches between them during battle. Allies act according to their assigned roles, allowing the player to concentrate on when to attack, defend or restore health. The right change can build an enemy's chain or keep the party alive.

cards.heading: From narrow routes to Gran Pulse
cards.text: Motomu Toriyama and Yoshinori Kitase described the early linearity as a deliberate choice, intended to introduce the characters and combat gradually. Freedom to explore and organise the party increases later, particularly on Gran Pulse. This structure divided players familiar with the towns and detours of earlier Final Fantasy adventures.

cards.heading: Faces and materials at a new scale
cards.text: The move to high-definition consoles required more detailed textures, materials and expressions. Toriyama recalled the art team learning to sustain close views of skin and clothing. Character performances and elaborate battles place those production changes at the centre of the game's presentation.

main.title: Guitar Hero: Van Halen
main.subtitle: One band, four instruments
main.summary: Van Halen’s early repertoire becomes a full-band rhythm game, with Eddie’s guitar solos at its centre.

cards.heading: A catalogue built around Roth
cards.text: Guitar Hero: Van Halen brings lead guitar, bass, drums and vocals to the band’s repertoire. Twenty-five Van Halen songs and three Eddie Van Halen guitar solos appear alongside nineteen songs by other artists. The selection concentrates on the David Lee Roth era rather than covering every period of the group. The playable band reflects the 2009 line-up, including Wolfgang Van Halen; earlier appearances can be unlocked, but former members are not playable.

cards.heading: Four parts on the same stage
cards.text: Underground Development built the game around the full-band format of World Tour and Metallica. Eddie's solos supply demanding guitar passages, with the other instruments supporting shared performances. A North American Guitar Hero 5 promotion delivered copies ahead of the December 22, 2009 retail release.

main.title: E3 2010
main.subtitle: Motion control and new screens at E3
main.summary: On June 15, 2010 E3 opens its doors at the Los Angeles Convention Center as the major platforms try to redefine the relationship between body, screen and controller.

cards.heading: New controls and displays
cards.text: E3 opened at the Los Angeles Convention Center on June 15, 2010. Microsoft promoted Kinect for Xbox 360, Nintendo demonstrated the glasses-free 3DS and Sony presented PlayStation Move alongside stereoscopic games. The event brought different approaches to movement and display together as the console makers sought new audiences.

cards.heading: Kinect reads the body
cards.text: Kinect places a sensor in front of the television to read the player's body without a handheld controller. Demonstrations show how gestures such as jumping or stepping sideways can become actions in a game. The system must recognise those movements and give clear feedback so players can understand its response.

cards.heading: Trying Nintendo 3DS
cards.text: Nintendo demonstrated 3DS on June 15 after announcing it earlier in the year as the DS successor. Alongside a glasses-free depth display, it added a Circle Pad, motion sensors, a gyroscope and cameras. The stereoscopic effect made hands-on demonstrations particularly important, as an ordinary video could not reproduce the screen's depth.

cards.heading: PlayStation Move and stereoscopy
cards.text: PlayStation Move combines a handheld controller with the PlayStation Eye camera. It preserves buttons and a physical grip while tracking hand movement. Sony also presented stereoscopic display as an extension of the PlayStation 3 experience, bringing changes to both control and the image on screen.

main.title: SKATE 3
main.summary: Skate 3 is a 2010 skateboarding video game, the third installment in the Skate series and the sequel to 2009's Skate 2, developed by EA Black Box and published by Electronic Arts.

cards.heading: A team in Port Carverton
cards.text: Skate 3 is a 2010 skateboarding video game, the third installment in the Skate series and the sequel to 2009's Skate 2, developed by EA Black Box and published by Electronic Arts. It was released worldwide in May 2010 for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360. The game takes place in the fictional city of Port Carverton, which embraces skateboarding, unlike considering it a crime in the second game. The player character goes by the alias "The Legend". After failing to "Jump The Shark", their goal becomes creating a successful skateboarding team. It is the player's goal to sell one million boards by completing challenges. The game introduced some new features including new tricks, a park builder, and "Easy" and "Hardcore" modes instead of just "Normal" mode.

cards.heading: Glitches, videos and a later revival
cards.text: Skate 3 received generally favorable reviews from critics. In 2014, the game's popularity increased because of Let's Play channels on YouTube, showcasing the game's humorous ragdoll physics and glitches. A sequel, Skate, was released in early access in 2025.

main.title: Darksiders
main.summary: Darksiders is a hack and slash action-adventure video game developed by Vigil Games and published by THQ.

cards.heading: Vigil Games introduces War, a Horseman of the Apocalypse
cards.text: Darksiders is a hack and slash action-adventure video game developed by Vigil Games and published by THQ. The game's inspiration is from the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse, with the player taking the role of the horseman War. The game was released for the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 on January 5, 2010, in North America, January 7 in Australia, January 8 in Europe, and March 18 in Japan. The Microsoft Windows version was released in North America and Australia on September 23, and in Europe on September 24. A parallel sequel, Darksiders II, was released on August 14, 2012.

cards.heading: A central hub opens through newly gained abilities
cards.text: In Darksiders, players control War, one of the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse, in a third-person perspective. The world is split into separate locations with many areas initially inaccessible until later in the game. The center of the world, The Scalding Gallow, functions as a hub where War is given new objectives and paths to unlock new areas, many of which require the use of newly-gained abilities to progress.

cards.heading: Chaos Eater and other tools meet puzzle-like boss encounters
cards.text: War begins with Chaos Eater, then gains weapons that change his reach and attack combinations. Blocking, countering and dodging matter alongside striking, while a revolver and throwing blade answer more distant threats. Objects in the surroundings can become projectiles, and a summoned horse later speeds travel and increases attack power. Larger enemies sometimes become temporary mounts before a finishing blow. Bosses turn these tools into specific problems: recognising which weapon or action can expose a weakness becomes as important as surviving the next hit.

main.title: Kingdom Hearts Birth by Sleep
main.summary: Kingdom Hearts Birth by Sleep is a 2010 action role-playing game developed and published by Square Enix in collaboration with Disney Interactive Studios for the PlayStation Portable, serving as the sixth installment in the Kingdom Hearts series.

cards.heading: Square Enix takes Kingdom Hearts to the PSP
cards.text: Kingdom Hearts Birth by Sleep is a 2010 action role-playing game developed and published by Square Enix in collaboration with Disney Interactive Studios for the PlayStation Portable, serving as the sixth installment in the Kingdom Hearts series. The game was released on UMD worldwide in 2010. An international version of the game titled Kingdom Hearts Birth by Sleep Final Mix was released in Japan in January 2011, featuring the changes made in the non-Japanese versions. A direct sequel, Kingdom Hearts 0.2: Birth by Sleep - A Fragmentary Passage, was released in January 2017 as a part of a bundle of games called Kingdom Hearts HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue.

cards.heading: Three journeys lead toward the missing Master Xehanort
cards.text: The game utilizes an overhauled battle system different from previous games in the series which features new elements. It is a prequel to the original Kingdom Hearts, taking place ten years before its events. The game centers on the journeys of Ventus, Terra, and Aqua, characters briefly featured in Kingdom Hearts II, in their quest to locate the missing Master Xehanort and protect the worlds from creatures known as the Unversed. The player has access to the three characters' different scenarios when playing.

cards.heading: Focus and Dimension Links add character-specific command systems
cards.text: The Focus gauge powers Shotlock attacks, which lock onto enemies in a first-person aiming view before releasing homing attacks. It refills as the player lands attacks and Deck Commands. Dimension Links temporarily replace the command deck with abilities drawn from a companion met during the journey. Filling the command gauge during a D-Link leads to a finishing move, with stronger levels available as the link develops.

main.title: VVVVVV
main.summary: VVVVVV is a 2010 puzzle-platform game created by Terry Cavanagh.

cards.heading: Turning gravity instead of jumping
cards.text: VVVVVV is a 2010 puzzle-platform game created by Terry Cavanagh. In the game, the player controls Captain Viridian, who must rescue their spacecrew after a teleporter malfunction caused them to be separated in Dimension VVVVVV. The gameplay is characterized by the inability of the player to jump, instead controlling the direction of gravity, causing the player to fall upwards or downwards. The game consists of more than 400 individual rooms, and also supports the creation of user-created levels.

cards.heading: A new codebase opens more platforms
cards.text: The game was built in Adobe Flash and released on January 11, 2010, for Microsoft Windows and OS X. The game was ported to C++ by Simon Roth in 2011, and released as part of the Humble Indie Bundle #3. The port to C++ allowed the porting of the game to other platforms such as Linux, Nintendo 3DS, and Nintendo Switch. Unofficial ports of the game have been made for the Pandora and Commodore 64.

main.title: Last Window: The Secret of Cape West
main.subtitle: Kyle Hyde returns to another troubled address
main.summary: Last Window: The Secret of Cape West is Cing's Nintendo DS adventure following former detective Kyle Hyde a year after Hotel Dusk. Set in Los Angeles in December 1980, it places him inside the Cape West Apartments and another mystery connected with the people around him and his own past. The handheld is again held vertically like a book, giving conversations and drawn characters a distinctive presentation across its screens. Investigating an ordinary building gradually reveals a history that its residents have different reasons to explain, protect or leave unspoken.

cards.heading: Kyle Hyde returns to another troubled address
cards.text: Last Window: The Secret of Cape West is Cing's Nintendo DS adventure following former detective Kyle Hyde a year after Hotel Dusk. Set in Los Angeles in December 1980, it places him inside the Cape West Apartments and another mystery connected with the people around him and his own past. The handheld is again held vertically like a book, giving conversations and drawn characters a distinctive presentation across its screens. Investigating an ordinary building gradually reveals a history that its residents have different reasons to explain, protect or leave unspoken.

cards.heading: A useful question is not always the next one
cards.text: Conversations introduce an Ignore option, allowing Kyle to let a line of questioning pass when pursuing it would be unhelpful. Deciding what to follow therefore becomes as important as finding something to ask. An ill-judged statement, a suspicious possession or being discovered where he should not be can bring the investigation to an early end. The system gives encounters a social risk alongside the search for clues. Reading another person's reaction helps the player decide when to press forward and when leaving a subject alone is the more useful response.

cards.heading: The investigation leaves a book behind
cards.text: Completing a chapter opens another section of an in-game novel also called Last Window. Its account complements the events being played, with decisions affecting the material presented in the book. The device connects the handheld's book-like orientation with something that can actually be read after the investigation has moved on. Small optional activities offer further details of the period and the building's everyday life. The result gives Kyle's progress another form, allowing the same mystery to accumulate as both a sequence of conversations and an unfolding written record of the journey.

main.title: Valkyria Chronicles II
main.subtitle: Gallia's next conflict begins at school
main.summary: Valkyria Chronicles II is Sega's PSP tactical role-playing game, first released in Japan on 21 January 2010. Two years after the earlier war, military-academy cadets become involved in a struggle against rebels pursuing an ethnic-cleansing campaign. The school gives the story a continuing social setting between operations, while the battlefield retains the series' mixture of planning and direct control. The player selects a unit, then moves and acts from close behind it within the limits available. A tactical decision becomes something performed through the soldier rather than resolved entirely from a distant map.

cards.heading: Gallia's next conflict begins at school
cards.text: Valkyria Chronicles II is Sega's PSP tactical role-playing game, first released in Japan on 21 January 2010. Two years after the earlier war, military-academy cadets become involved in a struggle against rebels pursuing an ethnic-cleansing campaign. The school gives the story a continuing social setting between operations, while the battlefield retains the series' mixture of planning and direct control. The player selects a unit, then moves and acts from close behind it within the limits available. A tactical decision becomes something performed through the soldier rather than resolved entirely from a distant map.

cards.heading: Plan the turn, then move through the danger
cards.text: Command-level decisions determine which unit acts and how the available effort is distributed. Once selected, a soldier crosses the field under the player's control, making cover, distance and enemy fire practical concerns. Different classes provide different answers to an objective, encouraging the player to develop and use more than one kind of unit. The handheld format divides operations into compact areas, while the larger campaign supplies continuing progression. The player moves between thinking about the whole group and handling the immediate danger faced by the one character currently carrying out the plan.

cards.heading: A console strategy game finds a handheld form
cards.text: Takeshi Ozawa directed the sequel, with Hitoshi Sakimoto returning to compose the music. The PSP release offered a more portable version of the series' unusual combat while building a new cast around the academy. North American and European editions followed later in 2010, and reviews were generally favourable. Its setting changes the interval between missions: classmates and their development become part of the campaign's structure. The result is a distinct continuation, linking a war being fought outside the school to the young people learning how to take part in it.

main.title: Mass Effect 2
main.subtitle: The Suicide Mission That Made Consequences Part of the Cast
main.summary: Shepard recruits a crew for a suicide mission, with ship preparations and the loyalty of companions affecting who survives.

cards.heading: Preparing the suicide mission
cards.text: BioWare released Mass Effect 2 for Xbox 360 and PC in North America on January 26, 2010. Shepard assembles a specialist crew aboard the Normandy SR-2 for a dangerous mission against the Collectors. Recruitment, personal conflicts and preparations shape the finale, while combat becomes more direct than in the first game.

cards.heading: Shepard returns through Cerberus
cards.text: The opening destroys the original Normandy and leaves Shepard dead in space. Cerberus reconstructs the commander through the Lazarus Project, placing the familiar protagonist under the support of a suspicious new organisation. Imported decisions and relationships remain part of the journey, now seen from this changed position.

cards.heading: Recruiting the crew
cards.text: Dossiers lead Shepard to potential recruits including Mordin, Jack, Grunt, Thane and Samara. Each recruitment presents a different setting and problem, gradually filling the ship with specialists. Learning about the crew becomes part of the main preparation for the mission rather than a separate activity between story events.

cards.heading: Loyalty before the finale
cards.text: Companions bring unresolved concerns aboard the Normandy. Their loyalty missions address matters such as family, identity, revenge and responsibility. Helping them can improve the chance of success in crucial tasks during the finale. Conversations and personal missions therefore contribute to survival alongside practical preparations such as upgrading the ship.
